_comment: Portes du Soleil. Audit sign-offs, plus one hand-elevation patch at Avoriaz. See src/config/resorts.ts for the Roc d'Enfer exclusion box.
_comment_setNodeElevation: AVORIAZ VILLAGE PATCH - the case where BOTH sources are wrong, which is exactly what setNodeElevation is for. Our elevation provider reads this shelf 5-76 m TOO LOW, and the second DEM (Terrarium) reads it 3-7 m TOO HIGH, almost certainly sampling the tops of Avoriaz's tall timber-clad apartment blocks rather than the snow. Because neither source is competent here, the elevation-consensus pass DECLINES the whole 22-node patch (that is the atomic-patch guard working as designed - half a repair drops a step into the middle of the fault) and it can only be resolved by hand. Every value below was read off the contours on the debug map by the user, not derived. The load-bearing facts: the three lift bottoms Stade / Lac-Intrets / Tour are LEVEL with each other at ~1737 m (our data spread them over 17 m and put Tour 11 m too HIGH, which is why the links between them came out one-way instead of bidirectional), and Surf sits ~8 m above them at ~1745 m. DO NOT replace these with a DEM sample on the next refresh, and do not widen any tolerance to make the automatic pass accept this patch - it is right to refuse it.

setNodeElevation._why: Stade Tete au Boeuf (bottom) - the node the FIRST pass of this patch missed, and the proof that a half-patched fault is worse than an unpatched one: pinning the four lift bases around it left this one 17-25 m below them, every run bottomed out here, and it became a 22-node trapped basin that did not exist before. Read off the contours by the user like the rest.
Synthetic snap copies sit at their parent node's height - confirmed by the user's own readings for sn362907957 and sn7021400781, which both matched their parent exactly.

The same sunken shelf continues a few metres east - Retour Chavanette's bottom and the node beside Stade. Read off the contours by the user at ~1737-1738 m, i.e. level with the lift bases 27 m away, not 9-17 m below them.

Lift top station. The OSM point sits at ~1750 m where the cable enters the building; the skier exit is at ~1760 m, which is the elevation that matters for routing (this is the station the runs must leave FROM).

Prodains Express 3S top: the forecourt 11 m NE of the station, where the Crot and Bleue d'Arare stubs meet the arrival. Read off the contours as level with the station deck (1760). Our provider had it at 1737 and the second DEM agrees with 1751, but both are reading the ground beside the raised arrival platform, not the deck a skier stands on. Left uncorrected it was a DEAD END - six edges in, zero out - so every short run off the gondola top ended there and a skier was stuck.

Prodains Express 3S top: the Crot junction on the same arrival flat, 75 m SE of the station. Read as level with the deck (1760); our provider had 1765 and the second DEM 1759. This is what makes the Crot stub e2183 and the station link e4941 two-way, which is how the arrival actually skis - you can drift either way across the flat.

Prodains Express 3S top: the Bleue d'Arare stub end on the same arrival flat, 24 m N of the station. Level with the deck (1760). Left alone the elevation-consensus pass drove it DOWN to 1752 and the 21 m stub read as a 39% pitch.

Fornet chairlift TOP station, above Avoriaz on the Hauts Forts side. User read 2211 m off the contours - level with the Fornet junction n270740419 87 m SW, not 18 m below it. Both DEMs sample 2192/2193 here because they hit the ground beside the raised arrival deck, the same error as the Prodains 3S top. This was the resort's ONLY reversal candidate: at 2193 the only way in to n270740419 was an 18 m lift-access climb, which is exactly the shape check:elevation flags as a suspect elevation. At 2211 the 120 m Fornet link between them is level and two-way, and the flag goes away on its own.
Stade - bottom station, level with Lac-Intrets and Tour.
Lac-Intrets - bottom station, level with Stade and Tour.
Tour - bottom station. The only node in the patch our data placed too HIGH (1748 vs ~1737), which is why it never looked like part of the same sunken fault.
Surf - bottom station, ~8 m ABOVE the other three, not level with them.

acceptedDeadEnds.why: Bottom of the red 'Pauvre Conche' (w30751810) at 1826 m, which dead-ends mid-face under the Pauvre Conche chairlift. Reviewed by the user on satellite imagery and against published resort piste maps: there is NO visible snow connection onward, and no resort publishes a red run here - they list only the black '18 Pauvre Conche' and a blue of the same name. OSM tagging corroborates: w30751810 carries three tags and NO source, while the black w8215594 is source=GPS + piste:grooming=classic and the blue w274898287/w274898288 is source=Bing 2014, and both of those reach n616880 @1693 while this one does not. All three fork from the same top node n340096712 @1904. The nearest legal projection is 137 m onto the black and 17 m below it, i.e. just past rescueLineRadius (130 m). DELIBERATELY NOT BRIDGED: the rescue-radius-sweep re-measured 2026-09-07 found that raising the radius 130 -> 140 m admits exactly this one case fleet-wide with nothing else until 181 m, and the user rejected the change because there is no evidence of terrain in the gap. Most likely an unsourced OSM sketch; the honest fix is upstream. RE-CHECK ON REFRESH: a stale WARN here means OSM changed it, and this sign-off should be revisited rather than kept.

Top of runs '54' (blue) and '56' (red), Braitaz sector - OPEN OSM GAP, signed off pending an upstream fix, NOT a defect on our side. n13289373141 @1626 m has no in-edges at all; n13289373143 @1609 m is flagged only because its sole feed is that orphan. Below them everything drains normally (54 -> n281370219 @1570, 56 -> n7366125507 @1509). Verified: OSM w1448462122 ('54', easy) starts EXACTLY at n13289373141 (vertex 0, 0 m), so we imported it complete; elevations are sound (second DEM agrees within 1-5 m: 1626/1609/1570); there is NO abandoned:/disused: lift anywhere in the box, so unlike Torgon nothing was dismantled; and there is no other piste within 600 m of the top, nor any node higher than 1626 m within 988 m. The nearest lift, the Panthiaz gondola, tops out 348 m away and 139 m BELOW. The piste map has 54 served by Télésiège de Braitaz, whose top station (1799 m) in OSM only feeds the red 'Blanchot', landing 988 m away. CONCLUSION: OSM is missing the run - most likely a blue - that brings you from the Braitaz/Blanchot side across to the top of 54. Reviewed on the map by the user, who reached the same conclusion: real terrain, real missing feed, but we do not have the information to draw it. REJECTED ALTERNATIVES: (a) reversing the arrows so you enter 54 from the green below and climb to the top of 56 - that is 39 m of ascent over 425 m with the final pitches at 8% and 15%, far beyond maxTraverseClimb (8 m) and flatGradeMax (6%), and not a momentum traverse; (b) deleting the 145 m stub above the junction - it is part of OSM way 54 itself, so removing it just moves the orphan down to n13289373143. DO NOT invent a connector here. RE-CHECK ON REFRESH: if OSM gains the missing run these nodes stop being trapped and check:trapped will report this entry as stale - that WARN is the signal to come back and delete this sign-off.

Torgon / La Jorette (Swiss side) - the 2.1 km blue chain descending from 1621 m through 1503 / 1341 / 1329 / 1181 m to the two dead ends at 1142 and 1143 m in the Vionnaz valley. Reported as 5 trapped + 3 orphan nodes, but it is ONE connected descent, not eight defects. THE LIFTS THAT SERVED IT HAVE BEEN DISMANTLED, and OSM says so explicitly: w44538226 'Télésiège Jorette' is abandoned:aerialway=chair_lift, w45666705 'Télésiège Grands Places' is abandoned:aerialway=chair_lift, and w44538224 'Fignards' is disused:aerialway=drag_lift. Their positions land on the stranded chain itself - Jorette's centre (46.30924,6.86262) sits on n565736424 @1341 / n14050186237 @1329, and Fignards' centre (46.31198,6.86650) sits on n14050186233 @1181, the node feeding both bottom dead ends. Corroborated off-map: the chairlifts linking Torgon La Jorette to the main Plan-de-Croix area were decommissioned and the link is now shuttle bus only; just beginner lifts remain at La Jorette. So the pipeline is behaving correctly on every count - it imports the pistes (they are still drawn, and still skiable downhill) and refuses the abandoned/disused lifts. NEVER bridge this: any connector added here would fabricate a lift that no longer exists in the real world. Signed off by the user after review. UPDATE 2026-09-07: n14050186237 @1329 and n565736424 @1341 stopped being reported as trapped or orphan after the two-raster elevation rollout (they can now reach a lift), so they were removed from this list to stop check:trapped WARNing about them on every run. The terrain and the verdict are unchanged - they are named here so the record survives, and if a future rebuild re-strands them they belong to this same signed-off chain.

Morzine, foot of the 'Crôt' blue (1164 m). Reviewed on the map by the user: this is a run that legitimately ends AT THE HOUSES it serves - you ski in to your door and walk from there. Traced back, it is a continuous 1.2 km descent (Crozats black -> Crôt blue) off the Morzine side, and it stops 277 m from the nearest lift station and 10 m BELOW it, i.e. on the valley floor in the village, not short of a lift it ought to reach. Nothing for the pipeline to connect: there is no snow onward. Counted as 'trapped' only because a skier cannot ride back up from the doorstep, which is true and correct.

Châtel side, foot of an unnamed blue at 1327 m. Same call as the Morzine Crôt dead end above and reviewed the same way by the user: a genuine ski-in-to-the-houses run-out. It is the bottom of a continuous 2.4 km blue descent from 1840 m, ending 257 m from the nearest lift station and 15 m below it. Real terrain that really does end there, so it stays in the graph and routes normally; it is only removed from the audit's trapped count.

acceptedBasins.why: Mont Chéry, Les Gets (150 nodes, 4 lifts - Mont Chéry gondola, Chéry Nord, La Pointe, Rosta). Not a data defect: Mont Chéry is the north-facing half of Les Gets and is separated from the Chavannes half by the VILLAGE CENTRE. The two gondola bases sit 430 m apart at 1168 m and 1169 m - dead flat, no snow between them. Checked against OSM over the whole village box: there is NO conveying=* way (unlike Ortisei's La Curta escalator, which we do import) and NO piste:type=connection crossing the gap; the only ways there are ordinary highway=footway/steps/pedestrian and bus relations, including r6561122 'Ligne E: Lassare -> TC Mont-Chéry -> Le Nant'. The user correctly points out the crossing IS served - Les Gets runs a free Petit Train road shuttle continuously between the two gondolas, purpose-built for skiers with gear - but a road vehicle has no way of its own in OSM and is not fixed infrastructure, so there is nothing the pipeline could legitimately import. Same call as Ortisei (259 m across the pedestrianised main street) and Canazei ('the gap is a street, not snow'). USER VERDICT: sign off, add no synthetic link. The honest general fix is a 'village transfer' edge kind (official free shuttles as an opt-in leg with a declared wait), which would resolve Les Gets, Ortisei, Canazei and the Châtel bus gap together - tracked as a backlog item,       not a per-resort override.

Les Gets + Morzine-Pléney (446 nodes, 42 lifts - Pléney, Nyon, Chavannes, Ranfoilly Express, Chamossière Express, Perrières Express, Troncs Express, Belvédère, Charniaz Express, Crusaz ...), 981-1965 m. This is the French core of Portes du Soleil, and it is split from the main body (Avoriaz + Châtel + the Swiss side) by MORZINE VILLAGE. The detector's best link is 530 m and -17 m, from the Pléney/Crusaz run-out across the town to the Super-Morzine gondola base - the Pléney gondola is 195 m from the exit and Super-Morzine 276 m, on opposite sides of the Dranse. That is a street crossing, not snow, and in real life you walk it or take the free Morzine village bus. Note the detector itself says one link would free only 441 of 446 nodes, so even bridging it would not close the basin. Reviewed on the map by the user: this is an island, sign off, add no synthetic link. Same family as Mont Chéry and Super-Châtel in this resort - three village splits in one ski area, which is the case for the 'village transfer' edge kind on the backlog rather than three inventions here.

Super-Châtel / Morclan (197 nodes, 32 lifts - Super-Châtel gondola, Morclan, Barbossine, Petit Châtel, Panthiaz, Conches, Braitaz, Tour de Don, Coqs ...), 1011-1981 m. The north side of Châtel, split from Linga / Pré-la-Joux by CHÂTEL VILLAGE. The detector found no plausible link at all - its best candidate is 6828 m away and 127 m higher, which is its way of saying there is nothing there. That is correct: the Super-Châtel base and the Linga base are connected by the free Châtel village bus, not by any run. Reviewed on the map by the user: an island, sign off, add no synthetic link. Same village-split family as Mont Chéry and Morzine-Pléney.

La Chapelle-d'Abondance (48 nodes, 7 lifts - Crêt Béni, Fontaines, Bambi, Prés 1/2, Combe, Dahu), 996-1563 m. A small village ski area in the Vallée d'Abondance. It is a Portes du Soleil PASS member but it is not lift-linked to the circuit: the detector's best candidate is 4330 m away and 379 m below, i.e. nothing. Same situation as Monterosa's Antagnod and Roc d'Enfer - pass membership is not a lift link (see the precedent comment in src/config/resorts.ts). Reviewed on the map by the user: an island, sign off. Kept in the graph because it is real terrain inside the bbox; it is simply not reachable on skis.

Abondance (30 nodes, 8 lifts - Essert gondola, Corne 1/2, Petit Covagny, Grand/Petit Frémoux, Lac, Follys), 956-1677 m. The second small village area in the Vallée d'Abondance, same story as La Chapelle-d'Abondance above: a Portes du Soleil pass member with no lift or piste link to the circuit. The detector's best candidate is 370 m and -4 m from the Essert gondola base to a point part-way along the Ludoffaz run - a valley-floor crossing at the village, not a ski link. Reviewed on the map by the user: an island, sign off, add no synthetic link.

Géant + Snowly, above Châtel (4 nodes, 2 lifts). A self-contained beginners' pod, not a stranded sector - the same shape as Monterosa's Wold. 'Géant' is a 403 m platter with one 418 m blue beside it, and 'Snowly' is a 133 m rope tow with 18 m of vertical. The whole component is 4 nodes; the network is 294 m away and 1 m higher. Reviewed on the map by the user: ski-school terrain, nothing to connect, remove it from the review list as noise.
